answer: Canyon-range laser proof — a $24 violet-laser rangefinder guards each identity from a real canyon rim, hooded in velvet against stray sun. Each epoch it measures the wall across the gap; the verifier matches the distance against the canyon's USGS survey profile, and a reading from any other canyon misses the profile by metres and fails on the spot. If two identities point at the same gap, their readings match to the millimetre and the pair is struck together. The survey profile is public, so any grader can re-run the match — a fake has nowhere to hide its metres.
